text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 21-year-old man for ongoing management. He originally presented at 12 years of age with an early-onset, non-insulin-dependent form of diabetes, which had initially been managed with lifestyle modifications and low-dose oral medication.

Over the past several months, he has experienced deteriorating control, with home capillary fingersticks demonstrating persistent high blood sugar levels ranging between 180 and 230 mg/dL. His recent laboratory work showed a raised glycated haemoglobin of 8.7%. Autoimmune serologies were comprehensively non-reactive: he had no detectable antibodies to glutamic acid decarboxylase, and tests for both anti-insulin and islet antigen-2 antibodies were entirely negative.

Because of intermittent non-specific flank aching, he recently underwent cross-sectional abdominal imaging. This demonstrated marked diffuse parenchymal volume loss and shrinkage throughout the entire pancreas. In addition, multiple fluid-filled cysts were identified bilaterally within the renal parenchyma.

He is currently asymptomatic otherwise, employed full-time as a civil engineer, and does not smoke. On physical examination, he appears well and lean with a BMI of 22.1 kg/m². His blood pressure was 116/72 mmHg, cardiovascular and respiratory examinations were normal, and the abdomen was soft and non-tender. Routine serum chemistry, including his serum creatinine, urea, and electrolytes, was within normal limits.

I would be very grateful for your expert opinion and guidance regarding further clinical assessment and therapeutic strategies for him.

Sincerely,

Dr. Alan Davenport
